{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/trial.csv')

# Step 1: Deduplicate on patient_id, keeping the row with the highest sample_seq
# First, sort by patient_id and sample_seq (descending)
data_sorted = data.sort_values(by=['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False])

# Then drop duplicates on patient_id, keeping the first (highest sample_seq)
deduplicated = data_sorted.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Check: should now have 848 - 48 = 800 unique patients
print('Number of unique patients after deduplication:', deduplicated['patient_id'].nunique())

# Check assay_batch: batch B reports in µg/L, so biomarker_final must be divided by 10 to convert to ng/mL
print('\nUnique assay_batch values:', deduplicated['assay_batch'].unique())

# Convert batch B values to ng/mL: divide by 10
# Create a copy to avoid modifying original
deduplicated['biomarker_final_ngml'] = deduplicated['biomarker_final']

# Apply conversion only to batch B
deduplicated.loc[deduplicated['assay_batch'] == 'B', 'biomarker_final_ngml'] /= 10

# Check: verify the conversion worked
print('\nSample of biomarker_final_ngml after conversion:')
print(deduplicated[['assay_batch', 'biomarker_final', 'biomarker_final_ngml']].head(10))

# Now compute the mean of biomarker_final_ngml across all patients
mean_biomarker_final = deduplicated['biomarker_final_ngml'].mean()
print(f'\nMean biomarker_final (ng/mL) across all patients: {mean_biomarker_final}')"}
